summary_paragraph: A man with a history of end-stage renal disease due to diabetic nephropathy, failed kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and chronic pain was admitted for acute shortness of breath and chest pain in the setting of hypertensive urgency. He presented with a blood pressure in the 170s–200s and pulmonary congestion on imaging, consistent with flash pulmonary edema. His symptoms improved after intravenous furosemide and reinitiation of antihypertensive medications. Evaluation included a pharmacologic nuclear stress test, which showed stable coronary artery disease with a fixed inferior wall defect and preserved ejection fraction. His blood pressure regimen was simplified by discontinuing labetalol and chlorthalidone due to dizziness, and he was discharged on nifedipine alone. His anemia worsened slightly, likely due to chronic kidney disease, and follow-up was arranged with nephrology. He was also referred for a repeat sleep study, pancreatic MRCP, and renal MRI for ongoing management of comorbid conditions.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
